items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I got left behind with the Nat Towles’ band many times... I wouldn’t speak to Towles no more... I wouldn’t play with him or anything like that

ctx.x: No, I got left behind with the Nat Towles’ band many times because Towl would leave sometimes and it wouldn’t be nobody but him. If we was supposed to leave at a certain time he would leave, and he left us, left me and Henry Coker, who later became a great trombone player man, and he left us in DesMoines, Iowa or somewhere. And we went out and picked pockets, somebody picked pockets, and we got our money back and more. I © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

learned. And I tried to pull Coker’s coat you know, because I had seen this happen. You know whatever you say you get pickpocket, you had to make it good, so and I knew this and I had seen this happen you know? So I think we got pickpocket for about $15 apiece, but no money man, you know? So we wake up and everybody’s gone and the money’s gone, and when I went to the landlord of the house and told him that we didn’t have any money and what have you. So he cursed us out and everything. So I says okay. So I went on…
